reason: E1 directly states that high strength and strength retention in NbTaTiV are attributable to edge dislocations, supporting the edge dominance premise. However, the cited evidence does not provide specific data on the ~10–20% strength reduction, the thermal activation comparison between edge and screw dislocations, or the baseline behavior of conventional BCC alloys, leaving those premises unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Edge dislocation glide dominates in NbTaTiV at elevated temperatures (up to 1000 K)
Edge dislocations are less susceptible to thermal activation than screw dislocations in this alloy
This edge dominance causes only a modest (~10–20%) yield strength reduction at high temperature
Conventional BCC alloys (e.g., pure Nb) are controlled by screw dislocations and show a sharper strength drop
